fields.meta_title: Photo Contest Form Builder With Blind Judging | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a photo contest form that caps photos per category and shows judges entry numbers, not names. Photos save to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Photo Contest Form With Category Caps and Blind Judging
fields.hero_description: Build a photo contest form that takes each photo with its title and category, then shows judges entry numbers instead of names.
fields.features_heading: Entries Sorted Before the Judges Sit Down
fields.features_subheading: Describe your rules once, and Emergent builds a photo contest form that holds each entrant to them and gives judges a numbered set.
fields.feature_1:
A title and a category on every photo

Each upload carries a title and the category it enters, next to the entrant's name and email. Judges see what every photo is called and which category it belongs in.
fields.feature_2:
Entry limits for each category

Set how many photos one person may enter in a category. When someone reaches the limit in Nature, the form says so and offers the categories where they still have room.
fields.feature_3:
Judging by entry number, not name

The judges' screen shows each photo with its entry number and category. Names stay on the organizer's side, so a judge scoring a club friend's photo cannot tell it is theirs.
fields.feature_4:
A final round built from judges' stars

Each judge stars favorites on their own screen. Any photo with enough stars moves to the final round, and you set how many it takes, such as 2 stars from a panel of 3.
fields.feature_5:
Every entry in a database you own

Each entry becomes a row with the entrant, the email, the category, the photo, and its stars. Sort by stars to see the leaders, or filter to the photos no judge has opened yet.
fields.feature_6:
The code, exported to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the code for the form and the judges' screen to your GitHub repository. Host it with the rest of your club's site, or have a developer keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Clubs, Tourism Boards, Schools, and Rescues
fields.tab_content_1:
After 2 in Nature, Pauline's third photo goes to Monochrome

Kettle Rock Camera Club lets each member enter 2 photos per category in its monthly competition. Pauline Vashenko has 2 heron shots in Nature for October. When she uploads a third, the form says Nature is full this month and offers Monochrome, where she has 0 entries. She enters it there as Fog Over the Weir.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every photo names its park, and Cobbler Falls leads at 41

The Brisewood County Visitors Bureau asks every entrant to pick the park where the photo was taken, from a list of 6. Its entry table counts all 188 photos across the 6 parks. Cobbler Falls leads with 41 entries. Quarry Lake has the fewest, 22, and the bureau features it in the next newsletter.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 96 photos, 9 earn stars from 2 judges or more

Larch Valley High's art department received 96 photos for its spring contest, and 3 judges star favorites on a screen that shows entry numbers, never student names. Any photo starred by at least 2 judges goes to the final round. The final round holds 9 photos, led by entry 0583 with all 3 stars.
fields.tab_content_4:
Albertine chases February when it stalls at 3 entries

Cinderhill Animal Rescue is picking 12 photos for next year's calendar, one for each month. Every entrant picks the month a photo suits. Of 140 entries so far, February has 3 and July has 4. Any month under 5 entries is flagged for Albertine Marrow, the volunteer coordinator, who asks for snowy February shots.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Photo Contest Form
fields.howto_description: Use these 7 steps to launch a photo contest form that holds entrants to category limits and hides names from judges.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for five things per entry
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the rules above the upload button
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the contest in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the categories before you write a single field, such as Nature and Monochrome for a camera club. Then set the entry cap for each one, since the form's messages depend on that number.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the entrant's name, email, the photo, its title, and the category. Keep the name and email on the organizer's record, where they wait for the results email and any prize delivery.
fields.howto_step_3_des: State the deadline and the limit per category in plain sentences at the top of the form. Say whether edited photos may enter, and spell out where you plan to show the winning photos.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a few sentences for Emergent with the fields, the categories, the limit, and the judging rule. Emergent builds the form and the entry database from that prompt, and a later rule change is one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give every judge one method, stars or points, and write down how many a photo needs to reach the final round. With 3 judges, a bar of 2 stars means a photo needs a majority of the panel.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Upload a photo, then a second and a third in the same category, and check that the third gets the full-category message. Open the judges' screen and confirm your own name does not appear on it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link, then the results
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the form link in your newsletter and on your website. When judging closes, the app emails every entrant the results from the same entry list the judges scored.

faq_plan.q: What is a photo contest form?
faq_plan.a: A photo contest form is the online form entrants use to submit photos to a contest. It saves each upload as a numbered entry with the entrant's details, and the organizer judges from that one list instead of an inbox of attachments.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a photo contest form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the contest in Emergent's AI form builder: the categories, the limit per entrant, and how judges score. For example: "Build a photo contest form for my garden club with 3 categories and 2 photos per category." Emergent turns that sentence into the form and the table behind it, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How many photos should a photo contest form let each entrant submit?
faq_plan.a: Allow 2 or 3 per category for a club contest, then check the total against your judges' time. A club of 60 members entering 2 photos in each of 3 categories can send up to 360 photos. At 30 seconds per photo, that is 3 hours of judging for each judge. Lower the cap if that is too long.

faq_plan.q: Should a photo contest form offer more than one category?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once your entrants shoot different subjects. Make the category a required pick from a fixed list. Every photo then lands in exactly one, and judges score one category at a time. For a contest without a photo, such as a recipe or essay contest, a plain contest entry form is the better fit.

faq_plan.q: How do I hide entrant names on a photo contest form from judges?
faq_plan.a: Show judges an entry number in place of the name, then check what else gives the entrant away. A file named after its owner, or a title that mentions them, breaks the blind. Ask for each upload to be saved under its entry number, and keep the title as the only words judges read.

faq_plan.q: When should a photo contest form stop taking entries?
faq_plan.a: Close it at a fixed date and time, and print the time zone next to it, such as 11:59 p.m. Eastern on March 31. Leave at least a week between the close and the results so judges are not rushed. In a form built on Emergent, the app emails your mailing list a reminder 2 days before the close.

faq_plan.q: Should a talent search use a photo contest form?
faq_plan.a: No. A talent search judges the person, and a photo contest judges the picture. Use an audition form instead: it records the performer, the role they want, and when they can come in, with headshots attached to the application.

faq_plan.q: Can visitors vote on entries from a photo contest form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a gallery page where each photo shows its entry number and a vote button, and allow one vote per email address for each photo. Keep the public votes and the judges' stars in separate columns to name both a judges' pick and a people's choice. Forms built on Emergent have no response caps, and a vote that spreads past your members keeps counting.

faq_plan.q: Can one photo contest form run a new contest every month?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep one form and add the contest month to each entry. The limit per category then resets when the month changes. The entries live in a database you own: every member's past months stay in one table, and you can see who entered all season.

faq_plan.q: Where should I post a photo contest form so people enter?
faq_plan.a: Give the contest its own page with the prize, the deadline, and last year's winning photos, and put the form on that page. If the prize is the main draw and the photo is only the way in, a giveaway landing page fits better.
